steps.content: Eleanor turns out to be a skilled player. While you are still exploring the town with trepidation, she's turned the place upside down, chatting with each villager multiple times and extracting all their hidden information.

Eventually, even the frightening ghosts can't be bothered to appear before her. After sweeping through the town like an expert player, she's convinced she's finished her round prematurely and begins to stretch and yawn idly.
You walk over to Eleanor and examine the various items she's plundered from the villagers: letters, notes, small rings, oranges... even some villagers' clothing and other stuff...
In this type of game, ransacking everything like a bandit seems to be a perfectly acceptable behavior.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Yes?
Many of the written materials coincidentally document the villagers' thoughts about the Witch. You crouch down and start reading them.

Villager's Letter: The town hasn't been peaceful lately. Everyone says it's the Witch. To keep my child safe, I tried sending him to my cousin in the neighboring village. But... every night, the neighbors would bring my son back. I told them repeatedly he was not lost and didn't need to be sent back, but they simply wouldn't listen. After several attempts, there was nothing more I could do. What's more... I've noticed something wrong with my son. He doesn't seem like the same child anymore... I know this sounds unbelievable, but please come back and see for yourself. The child... he frightens me sometimes! Did... he...?!

Mayor's Notes: The fog in the town grows thicker each day. Unclean things lurk within it. Flowers in the forest have begun to devour people. The soil turns up putrid corpses. More and more people fall under the curse, transforming into corrupted monsters... This is the Witch's warning! The ward is crumbling. "Her" curse has seeped into every inch of the land. I know it. "She" has returned. The signs of doom draw near... For the town's peace, we must perform a sacrificial ritual immediately! Before the next blood moon falls, we must find a pure soul...

A New Interpretation of the Witch's Legend: At the kingdom's border lies a strange town shrouded in eternal fog and ravaged by disasters and curses. Legend says it's a forsaken land cursed by the Witch of Rewind. Many people leave their homes and arrive with desire and fervor, hoping the Witch could fulfill their wishes. The Witch hasn't chosen to stay willingly. People have trapped her here to harness her power. This "stolen" peace won't last forever. People must find a pure soul during the three moonrises and moonsets to quench the Witch's wrath.

Notes on the Foggy Town Written by: J. H., Traveling Scholar I've been here several days now. The fog is so unnaturally thick that it's impossible for one to tell the directions. At first, I thought this was just another ordinary remote town. But the more I know, the more I become unsettled. Tales about a Witch of Rewind prevail in the town. They say she can manipulate time and bestow peace. I initially dismissed this as mere folklore, a phenomenon not uncommon for a dwindling population whose faith has collapsed. But something is wrong. The roads at the entrance keep looping back. No matter which way I walk, I can't leave. I've observed that the townspeople all gaze up in the same direction at night... At a dark red moon. To anyone reading this: Do not enter the town after the fog rises. If you hear whispers around you, do not turn around. Run!

steps.speaker: Prima
steps.content: What are you reading?
Just as you're examining the writings, Prima suddenly peeks over your shoulder.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Some legends about a certain witch. Everyone in this village is terrified of her. We need to pass the Witch's Trial, and these might be our clues.
Come to think of it, Prima is also an NPC from here. Would she know something about the Witch in purple? Surely she won't be as tight-lipped as Rumina?
Prima tilts her head slightly, looking innocently ignorant.
Never mind. You sigh and return to the documents in your hands. The Witch, magic, wishes, and... the hourglass...
You find yourself instinctively looking up at the sky. You've never seen a moon shaped like this before. It's round, but somehow constricted in the middle, making it look more like...
An hourglass.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Has the moon always looked like this here?

steps.speaker: Prima
steps.content: Oh, I see. You're feeling homesick, aren't you? When you described the foreign world to me last time, I was absolutely fascinated! Could you tell me more about your life there? I want to hear more of your stories.
Prima stares at you intently with bright, curious eyes.

Noticing your animated conversation, Eleanor scoots over and perks up her ears to listen. The atmosphere feels perfect for a cozy chat, so you decide to share a few things, pretending you're telling bedtime stories to kids.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: My home... I suppose you could call it that. It has many floors and countless rooms. We usually relax in the common areas and celebrate holidays together.

steps.speaker: Prima
steps.content: Wow, you have a huge home! You never have to worry about coming back to an empty house. Someone will always leave the light on for you. I bet you never feel lonely, huh. That must be nice.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: My family... they come from all walks of life and have vastly different life stories, yet each of them is connected to me for one reason or another.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Most ordinary people fear them, but in fact, some of them are young girls just like you. They're not so different from anyone else.

steps.speaker: Prima
steps.content: I wish I could meet your family in the foreign world! If I could be friends with them... that would be really fun, don't you think?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: My line of work... it's a relentless job that is never done. I'm constantly being pulled into incidents that are either bizarre or dangerous.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I can't do it alone. It takes the combined efforts of many people to resolve these deadly situations every time.

steps.speaker: Prima
steps.content: No wonder none of this stuff scares you.
Prima appears thoroughly satisfied. Eleanor, however, is looking utterly bored again, kicking pebbles and muttering complaints under her breath.

steps.speaker: Eleanor
steps.content: Why are we the ones telling stories to NPCs now? This whole thing is getting dull. Turns out these "ultra-immersive thrills" they keep advertising get boring real quick. It's always the same predictable tropes. Once you've gotten used to it, you don't feel anything.

steps.speaker: Eleanor
steps.content: And here I thought there'd be some mind-blowing twist or something. Ugh, I'm ready to leave. It's like those haunted houses and escape rooms that just shuffle people in and out for cheap scares. It's so boring, so predictable. Can't they try something original for once? You know, give us special powers or something...

You see. Eleanor is one of those young Eastsiders who are tired of conventional routines and like coming to places like this for a change. But perhaps because your daily life already involves so much real danger, this leisurely experience with its refreshing theatrical tricks has actually been quite relaxing for you.
If it weren't for that strange hourglass and that shadowy figure you saw.

steps.speaker: Prima
steps.content: So, our great adventurer, do you prefer to live life on the edge? Is this not enough to satisfy you?
Prima asks seriously, pretending to extend a microphone toward Eleanor. Taking the cue, Eleanor plants her hands on her hips and responds firmly.

steps.speaker: Eleanor
steps.content: Of course! I paid good money to come here for something exciting I've never seen before! Look, don't take that personally, it's just that I was expecting something more! When I saw the posters, I thought this would be the next Witch Hall!

Prima looks pensive, muttering under her breath as she tries to commit both your and Eleanor's words to memory. This chat will likely end up in her little notebook and become her source of inspiration.
You suddenly wonder what kind of story Prima herself might have. As an NPC, she must have some kind of character profile or backstory, right?

steps.speaker: Prima
steps.content: Me? My story... There's nothing much to tell. Every day is pretty much the same... Hehe, if you're really that curious, next time I could...
Clank!
The sound of bells rings out from the town church as a crimson tinge spreads across the sky. Prima stops in her tracks, staring vacantly up at the night sky.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Prima, what's wrong?

steps.speaker: Prima
steps.content: Peaceful moments are always so fleeting... It's nothing. Let's go.
Prima forces a bright smile and hurries to catch up with you two.
